With an election next week where the White House sees foreign meddling
everywhere, it's launched a flagrant attack against freedom of speech on
supposed "national security" grounds.

Asked in a little-noticed Tuesday interview about what the government could do
about foreign influence operations on social media like TikTok, White House
counterterrorism czar Sebastian Gorka's
[reply](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rWC9VTW-rHc&t=2636s) was shockingly
frank:

> "We have that knee-jerk: 'Oh, First Amendment, don't do anything' -- but
> there are things we have to do if there's a threat to national security that
> actually comports with the U.S. Constitution."

When the White House's point man on counterterrorism calls First Amendment
concerns "knee-jerk," that's a pretty good sign that freedom of speech isn't a
top priority.

Gorka, as usual, is the car alarm in the coal mine, saying what the rest of
the White House is thinking but discreet enough to keep to itself. His
comments are an unusually blunt admission about what the federal government's
sprawling machine for combatting "foreign influence" is actually about:
censorship.

Officially, its job is countering Russian, Chinese, and Iranian operations
that might influence how Americans vote. The dirty secret is that the job runs
straight through the First Amendment -- if not the letter of the law,
certainly the spirit.

So who's the threat, in Gorka's mind? Tucker Carlson, the conservative
commentator who was once a MAGA enthusiast and ally of the president's, has
emerged as a critic over the Iran war -- an issue sure to be on voters' minds
next week. Gorka says the government has to do something "whenever he posts a
new anti-American interview," singling out his criticisms of the Iran war
specifically.

"Whether it's any of his recent rants about, you know, the justified war
against the Islamo-fascist regime in Iran -- watch the speed with which posts
like that are accelerated in ways that human beings can't …?" Gorka continued.

As he goes on to say, many online criticisms of the administration are "not
organic," but rather foreign influence operations aimed at "the duly elected
administration" -- a telling invocation of elections.

Per Gorka:

> "There are countries in whose interest it is to amplify artificially those
> voices that undermine the duly elected administration and commander-in-chief
> of the United States … Whether it's China, whether it's Iran, whether it's
> Russia, they want to see more of this. It's not organic, so they have to
> artificially accelerate it."

You'll notice he isn't accusing Carlson of taking orders from Tehran, Moscow,
or Beijing -- which is actually illegal. His argument is subtler and more
dangerous: because foreign governments might boost what Carlson says, what
Carlson says becomes a national security matter. By that standard, any
American critic of the war, or of the president, whose posts go viral is
potentially fair game for the counter-foreign-influence apparatus. And fair
game means subject to being shut down; or put another way, censored.

Trump's allies have been building this narrative for months, about criticisms
of the Iran war.

In March, Trump confidante Laura Loomer
[accused](https://www.mediamatters.org/laura-loomer/laura-loomer-accuses-
tucker-carlson-nick-fuentes-and-megyn-kelly-attempting-sabotage) Carlson of
trying to sabotage Republicans in the midterms. Before that, she had
[urged](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-summoned-break-vicious-
maga-184748303.html) then-Attorney General Pam Bondi to go after him as a
"national security threat."

In April, Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Trump's former press
secretary, [told CNBC](https://www.mediaite.com/media/news/sarah-huckabee-
sanders-rips-tucker-carlsons-dangerous-campaign-of-misinformation/): "The type
of misinformation that he's [Carlson] putting out on a daily basis is not only
wrong, but frankly they're dangerous."

Then in May, Trump went further and branded critical war coverage as literal
treason. "When the Fake News says that the Iranian enemy is doing well,
Militarily, against us, it's virtual TREASON in that it is such a false, and
even preposterous, statement," he [posted](https://www.mediamatters.org/fox-
news/trump-accuses-news-outlets-treason-fox-models-maga-iran-coverage). "They
are aiding and abetting the enemy!"

Notice how quickly the government's war on foreign influence blows back on
Americans. I've been warning about it all week in my series on the election
and the security apparatus around it: the military's Task Force Raider, the
Justice Department's Doomsday planning, and the National Guard's quiet
election mission. The government gets away with a lot by saying foreign,
foreign, foreign. But you can't study influence without studying who is
supposedly being influenced. And in this case, that's Americans.

None of this is to say foreign influence operations aren't real. Of course
they are. But so are corporate influence operations (called "marketing").
Companies spend fortunes trying to get Americans to buy what they're selling,
and they routinely flop. Think Apple's VR headset or Mark Zuckerberg's
metaverse. And those companies understand Americans far better, and are far
more competent, than, say, some Russian military intelligence unit. If Silicon
Valley's brightest can't make people want to buy something, why assume Putin's
drunk nepo hire (or whoever) can turn them against a war?  
  
Expect to hear a lot more about foreign meddling if the elections don't go
Trump's way, which polling suggests is likely. How's that for a Halloween
horror show?
